question: Can the unquantized FP32 whisper-tiny encoder run on the Hexagon NPU through ONNX Runtime QNN EP (enable_htp_fp16_precision=1, the default)?

local_compile_check.session.disable_cpu_ep_fallback: PASS - every node assigned to QNN EP

device: Snapdragon X Elite CRD (SC8380XP, Hexagon v73) via Qualcomm AI Hub

jobs.jg9zk7ywp: FAILED - Failed to finalize QNN graph. Error code: 6000 (qnn_model.cc:382 QnnModel::FinalizeGraphs)
jobs.jgdd8yqrg: FAILED - Failed to finalize QNN graph (same model, second device, reproduced)

same_device_a16w8_model: PASSED - 185/187 layers on NPU, 17.8 ms median (aihub_validation.json)
conclusion: Runtime FP32->FP16 conversion by QNN EP is not a safe path to the NPU on the device's QNN version, even though it compiles on a newer local SDK.
A local compile check can pass on a model the device rejects when the SDK versions differ; the real-device check stays the final word.
Qualcomm's own float Whisper is compiled ahead of time by AI Hub (--quantize_full_type float16) rather than converted at runtime by QNN EP.
